mainTopic: Selling what you don't own yet (רב and רבי מאיר), and whether found loan documents are returned (שמואל vs. רבי יוחנן)
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier discussion: the רבנן made a sale work out of concern for the seller's livelihood. Then רב rules that a person can sell a field he has not bought yet, and the sale takes effect once he buys it. רבא tries to limit this to 'a field' in general, but the גמרא rejects that limit, because רב follows רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer something that does not exist yet (דבר שלא בא לעולם). Next, שמואל rules that a found שטר הקנאה is returned to the lender, since we do not worry that it was already paid. רב עמרם tries to prove this from the משנה 'כל מעשה בית דין יחזיר,' but רבי זירא and רבא push the proof away. רבא explains that with seized land, a debtor who paid and did not get the document back caused his own loss, while with a loan note the lender may have held it back. רבי יוחנן then rules that even a court-ratified loan note found in the market is not returned, because we worry it was paid. The גמרא defends this against the same משנה and finally opens a side discussion about a כפרן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the previous discussion: concern for his livelihood
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the earlier discussion: the sale works because of concern for the seller's livelihood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of [concern for] his livelihood.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of an argument that started before this section. They give the reason the רבנן made a certain sale work: so the seller can support himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even where a sale might not work by the strict rules, the רבנן made it effective. Otherwise nobody would buy from this person, and he would have nothing to live on. With this, the earlier discussion is finished, and the גמרא moves to a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: His livelihood; what he needs to live on

phrases.english: because of [concern for] his livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם כְּדֵי חַיָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of the discussion that came before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sale is effective because of a rabbinic enactment based on concern for the seller's livelihood.

steps.title: רב: a field you will buy can be transferred now
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב: if someone sells a field he has not bought yet, saying it will belong to the buyer 'from now' once he buys it, the buyer acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: If someone says to his friend, 'The field that I am going to buy, once I buy it, is acquired by you from now,' the friend acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב rules that a person can sell a field before he owns it, and the sale takes effect once he buys it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller does not own the field when he speaks. Still, רב says that once the seller buys it, the friend owns it. The words 'from now' look back to the moment of the original statement.

keyTerms.meaning: It is acquired by you; it becomes yours
From now; the transfer counts back to this moment

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole debate that follows: can you sell something you do not own yet?

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
One who says to his friend:
A field that I am buying,
when I buy it,
it is acquired by you from now –
he has acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about selling property one does not yet own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person can sell a field he will buy in the future, and the buyer acquires it once the seller buys it.

steps.title: רבא limits רב to an unspecified field
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב's ruling only makes sense for 'a field' in general, not for 'this field,' because the current owner may never sell that one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב's ruling makes sense for an unspecified field. But for 'this field,' it does not work. Who says the owner will sell it to him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows רב's ruling. It works for any field, but not for one specific field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller promised 'a field,' he can buy some field, so it is in his power. If he promised 'this field,' he depends on the current owner agreeing to sell, so it is outside his control. To רבא, that makes it too uncertain to transfer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable; it makes sense
Who says? Who can be sure?

phrases.english: Rava said:
The statement of Rav is reasonable
with an unspecified field.
But with 'this field' – no.
Who is to say
that [the owner] will sell it to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִלְּתֵאּ דְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רב's ruling from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling applies only to an unspecified field, not to a specific field the seller cannot be sure of getting.

steps.title: The גמרא strongly rejects רבא's limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא insists, with an oath, that רב meant his ruling even for 'this field.'
steps.simpleTranslation: By God! רב said it even about 'this field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back hard against רבא. It says רב's ruling covers even a specific field. The next step gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath-like word והאלהים shows how sure the גמרא is that רבא's limit is wrong. רב's ruling is not limited to 'a field'; it also covers 'this field.'

keyTerms.meaning: By God! A strong, oath-like exclamation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read וְהָאֱלֹהִים as a new speaker or a story about God. It is simply a very strong way of saying 'I am certain!'

phrases.english: By God!
Rav said it even with 'this field.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאֱלֹהִים! אָמַר רַב: אֲפִילּוּ בְּ״שָׂדֶה זוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's limit from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's claim that רב's ruling covers only an unspecified field.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא's limit does not match the basis of רב's ruling, as the next step shows.

steps.title: Proof: רב follows רבי מאיר on things not yet in existence
steps.stepSummary: רב's ruling is based on רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can transfer something that does not exist yet. So even 'this field' works.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, whose opinion was רב following? רבי מאיר's, who says a person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it rejected רבא. רב's ruling rests on רבי מאיר's view that you can transfer things that do not exist yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allows even a transfer of something that does not exist at all. A specific field that the seller does not own yet is no harder than that. Once רב's source is clear, there is no reason to exclude 'this field.'

keyTerms.meaning: In line with whom? Whose opinion?
Something that has not yet come into the world; does not exist yet

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a field you will buy can be sold now, even a specific field. This is because רב follows רבי מאיר: אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם. רבא's limit to 'a field' only is rejected.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties רב's ruling to the larger debate over דבר שלא בא לעולם, a basic question in the laws of acquisition.

phrases.english: After all, Rav, in accordance with whom
did he say his ruling?
In accordance with Rabbi Meir, who says:
A person can transfer ownership of an item
that has not come into the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי רַב כְּמַאן אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reasoning behind the rejection in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רב's ruling applies even to 'this field.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's view that אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.

steps.title: The ברייתא: betrothal that can only work later
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists cases where a man tells a woman to be betrothed to him 'after' something happens that would make the marriage possible. The first opinion says she is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if a man tells a woman, 'Be betrothed to me after I convert,' or 'after you convert,' or 'after I am freed,' or 'after you are freed,' or 'after your husband dies,' or 'after your יבם does חליצה with you,' or 'after your sister dies,' she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing the actual source for step 5's claim about רבי מאיר. This is the first half of the ברייתא, which gives the opinion that disagrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case on the list, the man cannot marry this woman right now, but he will be able to later. The first opinion says קידושין that cannot work now do not work at all. This sets up רבי מאיר's opposite view in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Your יבם, the brother of your late husband

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
One who says to a woman
"Be betrothed to me after I convert,"
"after you convert," "after I am freed,"
phrases.notes: 'Freed' means freed from being an עבד. He is a slave and cannot marry her yet.

phrases.english: "after you are freed," "after your husband dies,"
"after your yavam performs chalitza for you,"
phrases.notes: She is a widow tied to her husband's brother. She can't marry anyone else until he does חליצה.

phrases.english: "after your sister dies" —
phrases.notes: He is talking to his wife's sister. He can't marry her while his wife is alive (ויקרא 18:18).

phrases.english: she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the ברייתא that step 5 relied on.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds a person can transfer something not yet available, even something specific.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: she is betrothed
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees and says the קידושין do work. They take effect once the obstacle is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: She is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the ברייתא. רבי מאיר says the betrothal works in all these cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a person can make a transfer now that takes effect later, even if it is impossible at the moment. Once she becomes available, the קידושין kick in. This is the idea רב relies on, as step 5 said.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that does not exist yet (the idea behind רבי מאיר's view)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
She is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין set to take effect after the obstacle goes away are valid.

steps.title: A specific woman is like 'this field'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a specific woman is just like a specific field. Since רבי מאיר says she is betrothed, רב's ruling must also work for 'this field.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And a woman is like 'this field,' and still רבי מאיר says she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof. It compares the ברייתא's case to 'this field' and shows that רב's ruling covers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had argued that 'this field' can't work, because its owner may never sell it. But a specific woman is just as uncertain: her husband may outlive the man, and she may never convert. Even so, רבי מאיר says the קידושין work. So רב, who follows רבי מאיר, holds that even 'this field' is acquired.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling works even for 'this field,' because רבי מאיר allows קידושין of a specific woman that can only take effect later.

phrases.english: And isn't a woman comparable to "this field"?
And yet Rabbi Meir said: She is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִשָּׁה כְּ״שָׂדֶה זוֹ״ דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי מאיר's ruling to the 'this field' case and closes the argument against רבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's ruling holds even for 'this field,' against רבא's limitation.

steps.title: שמואל: a found שטר הקנאה is returned
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. שמואל rules that someone who finds a שטר הקנאה in the marketplace should return it to its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Someone who finds a שטר הקנאה in the marketplace should return it to the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion with a ruling of שמואל about a lost document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר הקנאה is a document in which the borrower commits his property to the lender from the day it is written. שמואל says the finder gives it back to the lender. The next lines explain why the usual worries do not stop this.

keyTerms.meaning: A document committing the borrower's property to the lender from the day it is written
He should return it to the owner

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One who finds a deed of transfer in the marketplace —
should return it to the owner.
phrases.notes: The 'owner' here is the lender, who holds the document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַמּוֹצֵא שְׁטַר הַקְנָאָה בַּשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about found documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A found שטר הקנאה is returned to the lender.

steps.title: The worry that he never borrowed doesn't matter
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers the first worry. Maybe the borrower wrote the document but never took the loan. It doesn't matter, because he already committed himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the worry is that he wrote it planning to borrow but never did, he has already obligated himself.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains his ruling by answering a worry before anyone raises it: maybe the loan never happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a found loan document might be held back in case the loan never took place. Here the borrower committed himself the moment the document was written. So that worry no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it is because of

phrases.english: For if it is because he wrote it to borrow
and did not borrow —
he has committed himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי מִשּׁוּם דְּכָתַב לִלְוֹת וְלֹא לָוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains step 9 by removing the first possible worry.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The document might be worthless if the loan never happened.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שטר הקנאה binds the borrower from the day it is written, even without a loan.

steps.title: The worry that he already paid doesn't matter
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers the second worry. Maybe the loan was already repaid. We don't worry about that, because if it had been paid, the document would have been torn up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the worry is repayment, we don't worry about repayment. If he had paid, he would have torn up the document.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל removes the second worry, that the debt was already paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower who pays back his loan makes sure the document is destroyed. Since this one is still in one piece, we assume it was not paid. So it goes back to the lender.

keyTerms.meaning: He would surely have torn it up

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל returns a found שטר הקנאה because the borrower was bound from day one, and a paid-off document would have been torn up.

phrases.english: And if it is because of repayment —
we are not concerned about repayment,
for if it were so that he had repaid it —
he would certainly have torn it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִשּׁוּם פֵּרָעוֹן לָא חָיְישִׁינַן לְפֵרָעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the second possible worry and completes שמואל's reasoning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loan may already have been paid back.
steps.terutzMaskana: A borrower who pays would tear up the document, so we don't suspect it was paid.

steps.title: רב נחמן remembers the public announcement in שמואל's court
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן testifies that שמואל's court actually announced that found loan documents should be returned to their owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: My father was one of the scribes of the judges of מר שמואל. I was about six or seven years old, and I remember that they announced: Documents of transfer found in the marketplace should be returned to their owners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן shares a childhood memory showing that שמואל's ruling was really put into practice by his court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new argument. It is a report of real practice. It shows that שמואל's ruling from step 9 was not only theory, because his court publicly announced it.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribes of the judges, the court's writers
Documents of transfer, meaning loan documents that create a lien

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא מִן סָפְרֵי דַּיָּינֵי דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲוָה,
phrases.english: My father was one of the scribes of the judges of Mar Shmuel,
and I was about six or seven years old,
and I remember that they would announce and say:
Those deeds of transfer that are found in the marketplace,
should be returned to their owners.
phrases.notes: The owners here are the lenders, who hold the documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַבָּא מִן סָפְרֵי דַּיָּינֵי דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's ruling from steps 9-11 with an eyewitness report of how his court acted.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a found שטר הקנאה is returned
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's memory of the court's public announcement

steps.title: רב עמרם tries to prove שמואל's ruling from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם cites a משנה saying any court document is returned, which suggests we do not worry that it was paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: We also learn this in a משנה: Any court document should be returned. So it seems we do not worry that the debt was already paid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם brings a משנה as proof that שמואל is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says to return any court document without any condition. If we were worried the debt had been paid, we would not return it. So the משנה seems to agree with שמואל that we ignore that worry.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this, in a משנה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: אַף אֲנַן תְּנֵינָא.
phrases.english: Rav Amram said: We, too, learn this.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין – הֲרֵי זֶה יַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: Any court document, one must return it,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from a later משנה in this פרק (דף כ.).

phrases.english: Apparently, we are not concerned about repayment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a proof from a משנה to the support from רב נחמן's report.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that we do not worry about repayment
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: כל מעשה בית דין הרי זה יחזיר

steps.title: רבי זירא: The משנה speaks of documents that cannot be repaid
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rejects the proof: the משנה is about court documents of seized property, where repayment is not an issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: The משנה is talking about documents of foreclosure and seizure, which are not documents that get repaid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes back on רב עמרם's proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says to return certain court documents, the ones that give a lender rights to the borrower's property. Those debts are already settled through the property, so there is no worry about later repayment. That means the משנה says nothing about regular loan documents.

keyTerms.meaning: Documents of foreclosure that give property to the lender
A court document allowing the lender to locate and seize the borrower's property

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not arguing with שמואל's ruling. He only says this משנה is not a proof for it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:
The mishna is about bills of foreclosure and authorization,
which are not subject to repayment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַתְנִיתִין בִּשְׁטָרֵי חַלְטָאתָא וְאַדְרַכְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב עמרם's proof by limiting the משנה to a narrow type of document.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה, not שמואל's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with documents where repayment is not a concern, so it cannot teach about loan documents

steps.title: רבא: Even seized property can be bought back
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רבי זירא: seized property can be redeemed, for twelve months according to נהרדעא, or forever according to אמימר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Are these documents really not subject to repayment? The rabbis of נהרדעא say seized property returns to the borrower if he pays within twelve months. And אמימר said: I am from נהרדעא, and I hold that seized property can be returned forever.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רבי זירא's answer by showing that foreclosure documents can also be affected by repayment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said foreclosure documents are never repaid. But if the borrower can pay later and take his field back, then the document might be outdated. So the משנה still returns a document that might be paid, and רבי זירא's answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbis of the city נהרדעא
Property taken by court appraisal is returned

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: וְהָנֵי לָאו בְּנֵי פֵרָעוֹן נִינְהוּ?
phrases.english: Rava said: And are these not subject to repayment?
But didn't the Sages of Neharde'a say:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּמָא הָדַר עַד תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא.
phrases.english: Appraised property is returned until twelve months of the year.
phrases.notes: He means: if the borrower pays within a year, he gets back the field the court gave the lender.

phrases.english: And Ameimar said: I am from Neharde'a,
and I hold that appraised property is returned forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי לָאו בְּנֵי פֵרָעוֹן נִינְהוּ? וְהָא אָמְרִי נְהַרְדָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's claim that foreclosure documents are not subject to repayment.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that שטרי חלטאתא ואדרכתא are not subject to repayment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seized property can be redeemed by paying, so these documents can also become outdated, yet the משנה still returns them.

steps.title: רבא: In the משנה, the borrower caused his own loss
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new reason the משנה is no proof: a borrower who paid should have torn the document or gotten a new one, so any loss is his own fault.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: There, this is the reason: I can say that he caused the loss to himself. When he paid, he should have torn up the document, or else had another document written for the property he got back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רבי זירא's answer and gives his own reason why the משנה does not prove שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With court documents of seized property, a borrower who pays can protect himself by tearing up the document or getting a new document returning the field. If he did not, the loss is his fault, so we return the found document. With a regular loan, this reasoning may not apply, so the משנה does not prove שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier answer for a new one
He caused the loss to himself

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה is rejected. In that case we return the document because the borrower could have protected himself and did not.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, הָתָם הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: There, this is the reason:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה about court documents that רב עמרם quoted.

phrases.english: as I can say: it is he who caused the loss to himself,
since at the time that he repaid him,
he should have torn up his document,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי לְמִכְתַּב שְׁטָרָא אַחֲרִינָא עִילָּוֵיהּ.
phrases.english: or alternatively, to write another document about it.
phrases.notes: He means a new document showing the field was given back to the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, הָתָם הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי זירא's rejected answer with a new reason to reject רב עמרם's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב עמרם's proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה returns the document because the borrower caused his own loss, not because we ignore the worry about repayment in general

steps.title: Returning seized land is like a new sale, so the debtor needed a bill of sale
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains why a debtor who redeemed seized land should have had a new document written. By strict law the land stays with the creditor. Only because of 'the right and the good' did the רבנן say to return it, so the return is like a fresh purchase.
steps.simpleTranslation: By strict law, the creditor does not have to return the land. The רבנן said to return it only because of the פסוק 'Do what is right and good in the eyes of ה׳.' So the debtor is really buying it back from scratch, and he should have had a bill of sale written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבא's rejection from the last step. It explains why a debtor who paid off seized land should have had a new document written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting the land back is not a built-in right. It is a kindness the רבנן required, so legally it works like a new sale. A careful buyer gets a שטר זביני. If the debtor did not get one, any loss from the old document being returned is his own fault.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do what is right and good': the פסוק behind going beyond strict law

phrases.english: For by strict law, the land does not need to be returned,
and it is because of 'And you shall do what is right and good in the eyes of ה׳'
that the Rabbis said it should be returned.
Therefore, he is buying it anew, from the start,
phrases.notes: The debtor getting his land back counts like a brand-new purchase.

phrases.english: so he should have had a bill of sale written.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמִדִּינָא אַרְעָא לָא בָּעֲיָא לְמֶיהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבא's claim in step 16 that the debtor should have gotten a new document.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Supports the rejection of רב עמרם's proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה about seized land teaches nothing about worrying over payment. A debtor there who lost out caused his own loss by not getting a bill of sale.

steps.title: Can the same 'his own fault' reasoning work for a loan document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the same logic applies to an ordinary loan document. Can we say that if the borrower paid, he should have torn it up?
steps.simpleTranslation: With a loan document, what can we say? That if he paid, he should have torn up the document?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests whether רבא's 'his own fault' idea also covers a regular loan document. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a borrower who paid should always have torn the note, we could return found loan documents without worry. The גמרא raises this only to show that it does not work.

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי שְׁטַר חוֹב מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: Regarding a loan document, what is there to say?
That if it is true that he repaid it,
he should have torn up his document?

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי שְׁטַר חוֹב מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether step 17's reasoning carries over to ordinary loan documents.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can we blame a borrower who paid but did not tear up the note, the way we blame the debtor with seized land?

steps.title: The borrower may not have been able to tear it up
steps.stepSummary: No, the reasoning does not carry over. The lender may have put the borrower off ('tomorrow, it's not with me now') or held the note until the scribe's fee was paid. So the borrower is not at fault.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the lender was putting him off and told him: 'Tomorrow I'll give it to you, it's not with me right now.' Or the lender held onto it until he got the scribe's fee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea from the last step. A borrower who paid may have had no chance to tear up the note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With seized land, the debtor controls whether a bill of sale gets written. With a loan note, the lender holds the paper. So we cannot blame the borrower, and we still have to worry that a found loan document was already paid.

keyTerms.meaning: Held onto it, kept it back

steps.whatToRemember: Seized land: a debtor who paid can blame only himself. Loan document: the lender may have kept the note, so the borrower is not at fault.

phrases.english: Say that he was putting him off,
phrases.notes: The lender is the one dodging the borrower who came to get his note back.

phrases.english: saying to him: Tomorrow I will give it to you,
because right now it is not with me,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי אַפְּשִׁיטֵי דְסָפְרָא זָיֵיר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: or else he held onto it for the scribe's fee.
phrases.notes: The lender kept the note until the borrower covered what the scribe charged to write it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר אִשְׁתְּמוֹטֵי קָא מִשְׁתְּמִיט לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by rejecting the idea that a borrower who paid is always at fault.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects carrying the 'his own fault' reasoning over to loan documents.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The borrower may have been prevented from tearing up the note through no fault of his own.

steps.title: Even a court-ratified loan document found in the market is not returned
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes רבי יוחנן: someone who finds a loan document in the market should not return it to the lender, even if a court ratification (הנפק) is written on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone finds a loan document in the market, even if a court ratification is written on it, he should not return it to the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוחנן about a found loan document. This ruling is stricter, because it applies even when the court ratified the note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Court ratification proves the note is real and properly signed. רבי יוחנן says that still is not enough to return it. The reason is explained in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A court ratification written on a document, confirming it is valid

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבי אבהו said that רבי יוחנן said:
One who finds a loan document in the marketplace,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ הֶנְפֵּק –
phrases.english: even though a court ratification is written on it,
should not return it to the owner.
phrases.notes: The 'owner' here is the lender, the one who would collect with this note.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling on found loan documents after the discussion of רב עמרם's proof ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A found loan document is not returned to the lender, even if the court ratified it.

steps.title: Without ratification, the note may never have been used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the case without ratification is obvious. There, the borrower may have written the note planning to borrow and then never borrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Of course this is true where no ratification is written on it. There one can say he wrote it in order to borrow, but never actually borrowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining רבי יוחנן's ruling. First it shows why the case without ratification did not need to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A note with no ratification raises an extra doubt: maybe no loan ever happened. That makes it easy to see why it is not returned. רבי יוחנן's חידוש must be about something stronger, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not need to be said (the easy case)
He wrote it to borrow but never borrowed

phrases.english: It does not need to be said in a case where
no ratification is written on it,
for there one can say
he wrote it in order to borrow, but did not borrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא הֵיכָא דְּלֹא כָּתוּב בּוֹ הֶנְפֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 20 with the easier case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A note without ratification is surely not returned, since perhaps no loan ever happened.

steps.title: Even a verified note is not returned, because we worry it was repaid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's real חידוש is about a ratified note, meaning one the court has verified. Even that is not returned, because we worry that the loan was already paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even if a ratification is written on it, and what is that? That the note is verified by the court. Even so, he should not return it, because we worry it was paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי יוחנן. It defines הנפק as a court-verified note and gives the reason for not returning it: we worry about payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ratification removes the worry that no loan happened, but it says nothing about whether the loan was paid back. So רבי יוחנן sides with the view that we do worry about payment, as step 19 showed is reasonable for loan documents.

keyTerms.meaning: Verified by the court (the signatures were checked)
We worry that it was repaid

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, even a court-verified loan document is not returned, because we worry that it was paid.
steps.confusionAlert: הנפק does not mean the loan is still owed. It only proves the note is real and properly signed. The worry here is about repayment, not forgery.

phrases.english: Rather, even if a ratification is written on it,
and what is that? That it is verified by the court,
he should not return it, because we worry about repayment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ כָּתוּב בּוֹ הֶנְפֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation begun in step 21 by stating the real חידוש and its reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן holds that we worry about repayment, so even a verified loan document found in the market is not returned.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about court documents
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי אבהו from a משנה that says any document of the court must be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה challenged רבי אבהו: A משנה teaches that any court document must be returned!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks the ruling that רבי אבהו reported in the name of רבי יוחנן. He quotes a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that even a ratified loan note (one with a הנפק) is not returned, because the loan may already have been paid. But the משנה says any מעשה בית דין must be returned, which suggests we do not worry about payment. A ratified note is exactly the kind of thing the court has handled, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A court enactment: a document issued or verified by the court
He must return it to its owner

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised an objection to Rabbi Abbahu:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין הֲרֵי זֶה יַחְזִיר!
phrases.english: Any court enactment, one must return it!
phrases.notes: This is a quote from a משנה later in this פרק (דף כ.).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 22, which said that even a ratified note is not returned.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling (as reported by רבי אבהו) that a found ratified loan note is not returned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that all court documents are returned. That implies we do not worry about payment, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The משנה is about a known denier
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the משנה is talking about a borrower who is established as a כפרן, someone who denies his debts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said to him: ירמיה, my son, not all court documents are the same. The משנה means a case where the borrower is established as a כפרן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defends the ruling by limiting the משנה to a special case. The משנה only applies when the borrower is a known denier of debts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower has already been shown in court to falsely deny a debt, we do not believe him if he now says he paid. So in that case there is no real worry about payment, and the note is returned. In a normal case, רבי יוחנן's worry still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: My son: an affectionate way a teacher addresses a student
Established as a denier: someone shown in court to have falsely denied a debt

phrases.english: He said to him: Yirmeya, my son:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין שָׁוִים,
phrases.english: not all court enactments are equal,
rather, it is a case where he was established as a denier.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the borrower, who has already been caught lying about a debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ יִרְמְיָה בְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by limiting the משנה to a narrow case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers only to a borrower who is a known כפרן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that every court document is returned, with no concern about payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is limited to a known כפרן, whose claim of payment is not believed. רבי יוחנן's ruling holds for normal borrowers.

steps.title: A denier can still pay later
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רבי אבהו's answer: just because someone denied a debt once, does that mean he never pays?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Just because he was established as a כפרן one time, he will never pay at all?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer given in the previous step. He argues that being a denier does not remove the worry that the loan was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's answer assumed that a known כפרן's note can be returned because he surely did not pay. רבא points out that even a person who once lied may still have paid this debt. So the worry about payment remains, and the answer does not work.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And because he was established as a denier one time,
he will never again pay at all?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וּמִשּׁוּם דְּהוּחְזַק כַּפְרָן חֲדָא זִמְנָא תּוּ לָא פָּרַע כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's limitation of the משנה to a known כפרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Denying a debt once does not prove that a person never pays. The concern of payment still exists, so the note should still not be returned.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה is about foreclosure documents
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer. The משנה is talking about a שטר חלטאתא and an אדרכתא, court documents that are not subject to repayment, following רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The משנה is talking about a bill of foreclosure and a bill of authorization, in line with רבי זירא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבי ירמיה's challenge in a different way. He explains that the 'court documents' in the משנה are special collection documents, not ordinary loan notes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר חלטאתא and an אדרכתא are the court collection documents רבי זירא named in step 14. רבא himself showed in step 15 that seized land can still be bought back. So the point is his reason from steps 16-17: a debtor who paid should have torn up the document or gotten a new one, so any loss is his own fault. The משנה therefore does not contradict רבי יוחנן, who was talking about an ordinary ratified loan note.

keyTerms.meaning: Bill of foreclosure: a court document finalizing the transfer of the debtor's property to the lender
Bill of authorization: a court document allowing the lender to find and seize the debtor's property

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'court documents are returned' refers to collection documents like a שטר חלטאתא and an אדרכתא, not to ordinary loan notes. So רבי יוחנן's worry about payment for a ratified loan note still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up a ratified loan note (with a הנפק) with these collection documents. Both come from the court, but only with the collection documents does a debtor who paid have himself to blame for not getting the document back.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The mishna is about a bill of foreclosure and a bill of authorization,
and in accordance with Rabbi Zeira.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי זירא's answer earlier (step 14), which named these same two documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: מַתְנִיתִין בִּשְׁטַר חַלְטָאתָא וְאַדְרַכְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי אבהו's answer in step 25, רבא answers step 23's challenge a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers to collection documents, not loan notes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to require returning all court documents, including ratified loan notes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only covers a שטר חלטאתא and an אדרכתא, where a debtor who paid caused his own loss (steps 16-17), so it does not contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the challenge to רבי יוחנן and makes clear which court documents may be returned when found.

steps.title: Opening a side topic about a denier
steps.stepSummary: Since the topic of a כפרן came up, the גמרא decides to say something more about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about a כפרן: since the subject has come up, let us say something about it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is moving to a side discussion about a כפרן and is preparing to quote a teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כפרן was mentioned in רבי אבהו's answer, which was rejected. The גמרא still uses the mention as a chance to teach related laws about who counts as a denier. Nothing is ruled here yet; this line only introduces what comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it has come to our hands: a formula for starting a side topic

phrases.english: And a denier,
since it has come to our hands,
let us say something about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַפְרָן, הוֹאִיל וַאֲתָא לִידַן נֵימָא בֵיהּ מִלְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the term כפרן from step 24 and opens a side discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is a transition that introduces a discussion about the laws of a כפרן.

steps.title: רב נחמן: when the court says 'Go, give him'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר מניומי begins quoting רב נחמן about a case where the court told a litigant, 'Go, give him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: If the court said to him, 'Go, give him'…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting רב נחמן's teaching about when someone becomes a כפרן. This amud only gives the opening case, and the statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about a court that ruled against a litigant and told him to pay. The law about what happens next, and whether he becomes a denier, has not yet been stated. Keep the case in mind for the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: Go, give him: the court's instruction to the losing side to pay

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: As Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Nachman said:
If they said to him: "Go, give him,"
phrases.notes: 'They' is the court, speaking to the person they ruled against. The sentence keeps going on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the teaching that step 27 promised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening case of רב נחמן's teaching: the court told the litigant 'Go, give him.' The ruling itself continues on the next amud.
